prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: I can’t name one universal “best” company for everyone — the right HVAC contractor depends on your exact location in the Atlanta area, budget, the size and type of system you need, timing, and whether you need duct work or permits. If you tell me your ZIP code, the kind of system you have now (central AC, heat pump, age/size), and your budget/timeline, I’ll give you a short, practical shortlist plus help comparing quotes.

Meanwhile, here’s a quick guide to pick the best HVAC company to replace your air conditioner in Atlanta.

What to look for in a contractor
- Valid credentials: EPA 608 certification (for refrigerant handling), and confirm the company carries appropriate Georgia/local licensing and insurance.  
- NATE-certified technicians (Nationally recognized HVAC tech certification).  
- Good local reviews (Google, Yelp, BBB, Angi) and verifiable references from recent installs.  
- Written, itemized estimates (equipment model, SEER rating, tonnage, labor, permits, disposal).  
- Proper sizing (Manual J load calculation) and system design — low price + undersized or oversized unit is a common problem.  
- Clear warranty: manufacturer parts warranty plus a labor/installation warranty (ask length and what voids it).  
- Permits and code compliance: company should pull required permits and arrange inspections.  
- Financing and rebate assistance: whether they help with utility or manufacturer rebates and financing if you need it.

Questions to ask every contractor
- Are your techs NATE-certified? Are you licensed and insured in Georgia?  
- Do you perform a Manual J load calculation for sizing?  
- Which brand and model do you recommend and why? What is the SEER rating?  
- What is included in the written price (replacement of pad, thermostat, disconnect, permits, hauling away old unit, duct sealing)?  
- What are the warranties (parts, compressor, labor)? Any maintenance required to keep warranty valid?  
- Can you show recent references or photos of similar installs?  
- Timeline: how soon can you start, and how long will install take?  
- Do you offer financing or help with rebates?

Red flags
- Contractor who gives a firm price over the phone without visiting.  
- High-pressure sales pushing oversized systems or add-ons you didn’t ask for.  
- No written, itemized estimate or no permits.  
- Extremely low price with “we’ll see what happens” language — often leads to cut corners or hidden fees.

Typical cost and timeline (Atlanta area ballpark)
- Typical full replacement of a central AC (including outside condensing unit + indoor coil/air handler) commonly ranges roughly $3,500–$10,000 depending on size, efficiency (SEER), brand, and duct work. High-efficiency or multi-stage systems can be $8,000–$12,000+.  
- Most standard installs take 1–3 days once work starts. If ductwork, structural changes or permits/inspection backlog are involved, plan for more time.

How I can help now
- If you give your ZIP code and a few details (existing system type, square footage or tonnage, budget/timeline), I’ll prepare a checklist and a short list of recommended steps and a sample email/script to request and compare three written quotes.  
- If you already have 1–3 written estimates, paste them here and I’ll compare them line-by-line and point out issues.

Which companies are popular in Atlanta?
- There are several reputable local and national HVAC providers that operate in the Atlanta area; which is best for you will depend on the points above. Tell me your ZIP code and I’ll tailor recommendations and help you pick 3 good contractors to call.
